title: Runbooks, triage and the incident routine
summary: What a runbook holds, the first five minutes of a page, mitigate before you diagnose, the roles in an incident, and the timeline a blameless review is built on.

steps.title: A runbook you can follow at 3 a.m.
body: Every paging alert links a runbook. A good one is short and concrete:
1. **What it means** for users, in one sentence ("checkouts are failing faster than the SLO allows").
2. **First checks**, as links and commands: the dashboard, the Jaeger search for `error=true` on that route, the Loki query, recent
deploys (`kubectl rollout history`), the dependency's status page.
3. **Mitigations**, safest first: roll back the last deploy, scale up, turn off a feature flag, fail over, shed load.
4. **Escalation**: who owns the dependency, when to call them.
The first five minutes of a page: **acknowledge** (so nobody else starts in parallel), look at the **scope** (one route or all, one
region or all, since when), check **what changed** (deploys, config, flags, traffic), then **mitigate**. Restoring service comes
before finding the root cause: a rollback that fixes it in two minutes beats a perfect diagnosis in forty. The trace below is
where the lab's checkout incident starts: one red path, one log line with the code.

attrs.db.query.text: UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - $1 WHERE product_id = $2 AND qty >= $1
attrs.db.system.name: postgresql

logs.body: Reservation failed for sku 12: stock conflict in warehouse eu-2 (code INV-5821)

steps.prompt: You are paged: `CheckoutErrorBudgetBurn`. Put the first steps in order.
lines: Acknowledge the page so the team knows someone is on it
Open the dashboard: which route, since when, how bad
Check what changed: deploys, config, feature flags in the last hour
Confirm recovery on the same burn-rate panel
Post an update in the incident channel with the trace id that shows the failure
also: Acknowledge the page so the team knows someone is on it
Open the dashboard: which route, since when, how bad
Check what changed: deploys, config, feature flags in the last hour
Post an update in the incident channel with the trace id that shows the failure
Confirm recovery on the same burn-rate panel

steps.prompt: Errors started at 13:05, a deploy went out at 13:04, and you have a promising theory about a database lock. What do you do first?
options: Roll back the 13:04 deploy, then investigate with the pressure off
Investigate the lock theory until you are sure
Wait for the alert to resolve on its own
steps.explain: Correlated change + a cheap, reversible mitigation = do it now. If the rollback does not help, you have learnt something too. Restarting a database is neither cheap nor obviously related.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: on-call
steps.body: The commands you use during and right after a page.

toolkit.cmd: amtool silence add alertname=X service=checkout --duration=2h --comment='migration OPS-88'
toolkit.what: Silence a known, planned alert with an end and a reason.
flags: who and why: the next on-call reads it
toolkit.example: amtool --alertmanager.url=http://alertmanager:9093 silence add alertname=DiskFillingUp instance=db-1 --duration=4h --comment='resize in progress, OPS-88'
toolkit.when: planned maintenance, never to make an incident quiet

toolkit.what: What is firing right now, as Alertmanager sees it (after grouping and inhibition).
toolkit.when: "why didn't I get paged for X?"

toolkit.what: Roll back to the previous ReplicaSet: the most common mitigation.
toolkit.example: kubectl rollout history deployment/shop && kubectl rollout undo deployment/shop && kubectl rollout status deployment/shop --timeout=120s

toolkit.what: Pull failing traces from a script or runbook instead of clicking.
toolkit.when: a runbook step: "show me three failing requests"

steps.prompt: Match the incident role to its job.
pairs: decides, delegates, keeps the timeline; does not debug
status page and stakeholder updates on a schedule
writes down who did what, when, with links to graphs

steps.title: Build the incident timeline
prompt: The review starts from a timeline. Events come from several tools: `record Event(string At, string Source, string Text);` with `At`
- sorted by time (ties keep the input order);
- consecutive `log` events with the **same text** collapse into one line, ending ` (×{n})` when n > 1;
- the first `alert` line gets the suffix `" <- detected {m} min after the first deploy before it"` when there is a deploy earlier
(minutes rounded down; skip the suffix otherwise).
solution: var sorted = events.Select((e, i) => (e, i)).OrderBy(x => TimeSpan.Parse(x.e.At)).ThenBy(x => x.i).Select(x => x.e).ToList();
while (e.Source == "log" && i + 1 < sorted.Count && sorted[i + 1].Source == "log" && sorted[i + 1].Text == e.Text) { n++; i++; }
line += $" <- detected {(int)(TimeSpan.Parse(e.At) - TimeSpan.Parse(deploy.At)).TotalMinutes} min after the first deploy before it";
hints: Sort with the index as a tie-breaker: `events.Select((e, i) => (e, i)).OrderBy(x => TimeSpan.Parse(x.e.At)).ThenBy(x => x.i)`.
Collapse with an inner `while` that looks at the next event.
template: new("13:05:02", "log", "Reservation failed for sku 12: stock conflict (code INV-5821)"),
new("13:05:02", "log", "Reservation failed for sku 12: stock conflict (code INV-5821)"),
new("13:05:09", "log", "Reservation failed for sku 12: stock conflict (code INV-5821)"),
"13:05:02 [log] Reservation failed for sku 12: stock conflict (code INV-5821) (×3)",
"13:07:30 [alert] CheckoutErrorBudgetBurn firing (burn 67x) <- detected 3 min after the first deploy before it",
Dojo.Eq("no deploy, no suffix", new List<string> { "01:00:00 [alert] DiskFull" }, Timeline([new("01:00:00", "alert", "DiskFull")]));
record Event(string At, string Source, string Text);

steps.title: Live lab: the service that went dark
steps.prompt: In the live lab **OpenTelemetry on-call**, find out why inventory sends no telemetry and fix its exporter settings (task 4), then make its traces complete again with the right sampler (task 5).
steps.explain: Missing telemetry is an incident too: alert on it.
